# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date this letter is sent]

**To:** Harvard Pilgrim Health Care — Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Harper Delgado
Member ID: W267205200
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-09 — Reference number POC-E2AA78E9EC-43782**
**Service denied:** Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
**Plan:** Harvard Pilgrim Health Care (Commercial/ACA), State of Maine
**Governing policy:** Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316) — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2024-02/2023%20Knee%20Arthroscopy%20Clin%20Tip%20Sheet%20Evolent%2002282024.pdf

---

Dear Member Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), issued on 2026-08-09 under reference number POC-E2AA78E9EC-43782. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am respectfully asking the plan to reconsider that decision. My surgeon, Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and the records already in the prior authorization packet address the categories of information the plan's own tip sheet says a reviewer should look for.

I am asking for this appeal to be reviewed under the Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316), linked above, so that the reviewer and I are looking at the same document.

## The tip sheet identifies the information a reviewer needs — and my records contain it

The plan's tip sheet states:

> "The guidelines should be reviewed for additional requirements including duration of symptoms, physical examination, and radiographic criteria and for the complete listing of other procedures not included below."

Each of those three categories is documented in my chart:

**Duration of symptoms.** My records document 18 months of progressive pain in the knee, unrelieved by rest.

**Physical examination.** My exam findings are documented as positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. My records also document locking and giving way, inability to squat or kneel, and walking limited to level surfaces.

**Imaging.** MRI of the knee dated 2026-07-14 shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, with articular cartilage preserved and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1.

My records additionally document that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## My documented non-operative care matches the measures the tip sheet lists

I want to be straightforward with the reviewer about one point. The non-operative treatment lists I was able to locate in the tip sheet appear under headings for other arthroscopic procedures, and I have not been given plan language setting out a separate list specific to CPT 29881. I am therefore not claiming that the passages below are the exact criteria applied to my request. I quote them because they show the kinds and durations of conservative care the plan itself regards as meaningful, and my records document that care.

The tip sheet states:

> "(Evolent Guideline 316) 5— Knee Arthroscopy Clinical Tip Sheet ❖ Lateral Release • Failure of at least 6 months of non-operative treatment, including quadriceps strengthening and appropriate hamstring/IT band stretching and patellar mobilization techniques, and at least one of the following:"

and continues:

> "o Rest or activity modifications/limitations o Ice/heat o Protected weight bearing o Pharmacologic treatment:"

> "oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol o Brace/orthosis o Physical therapy modalities o Supervised home exercise o Weight optimization o Corticosteroid injection ❖ Debridement chondroplasty for patellofemoral chondrosis • Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following:"

Measured against those listed measures, my records document the following:

| What the tip sheet lists | What my records show |
| --- | --- |
| Physical therapy modalities; quadriceps strengthening | Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 14 weeks, 2026-03-26 to 2026-07-02, 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note |
| Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS | NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief |
| Corticosteroid injection | Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-13, giving 2 weeks of partial relief |
| Rest | 18 months of progressive pain unrelieved by rest |

That is more than one, and more than two, of the listed measures, over a period longer than 12 weeks of documented supervised therapy, on top of 18 months of symptoms. The records also show that this care did not resolve my symptoms.

## The imaging in my record is consistent with how the tip sheet treats arthritis

The tip sheet states:

> "MRI should not be the primary tool used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint."

and sets out a grading table:

> "Grade Description 0 No radiographic features of osteoarthritis 1 Possible joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation 2 Definite osteophyte formation with possible joint space narrowing 3 Moderate multiple osteophytes, definite narrowing of joint space, some sclerosis and possible deformity of bone contour 4 Large osteophytes, marked narrowing of joint space, severe sclerosis and definite deformity of bone contour"

My records report Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 with articular cartilage preserved. The problem my surgeon has documented is not arthritis — it is a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. If the reviewer requires a plain radiograph rather than the MRI for the arthritis grading described above, I ask that the plan tell me so specifically and allow it to be submitted, rather than close the request as incomplete. [If radiographs exist in my chart, list date and report here.]

## What I am asking for

The denial says the file was incomplete, but it does not tell me which document or data point was missing. The information the tip sheet points a reviewer toward — duration of symptoms, physical examination, and imaging — is in the packet, along with a documented course of conservative care and my surgeon's determination that surgery is needed.

I ask that the plan:

1. Overturn the denial of CPT 29881 and authorize the procedure; or
2. If the plan still considers the file incomplete, identify in writing the specific document or clinical element that is missing, and the specific criterion it relates to, so my surgeon's office and I can supply it promptly.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-05**, and I am submitting it within that period. I am sending this to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I can also be reached through Member Services at 1-888-333-4742 if the plan needs anything further from me.

I am enclosing, for the reviewer's convenience: [list enclosures — e.g., physical therapy discharge note dated 2026-07-02; MRI report dated 2026-07-14; office notes from Reyes, MD; injection record dated 2026-05-13; copy of the denial notice].

Thank you for taking another look at this. I would very much like to get back to walking, kneeling, and moving without my knee locking on me.

Sincerely,

**Harper Delgado**
Member ID: W267205200
Reference number: POC-E2AA78E9EC-43782
[Signature]
[Date]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
